record.paper_title: Heavy flavors and quarkonia: highlights, open questions, and perspectives
record.original_question: For charm quarks produced by hard scattering in a quark–gluon plasma, how completely and on what time scale do they approach local kinetic equilibrium compared with light degrees of freedom, and under which diffusion-coefficient conditions is a fluid-dynamic description of charm valid for a sizeable fraction of the deconfined fireball lifetime?

evidence.quote: Charm and beauty quarks, which are produced via hard scattering processes and have a much larger mass than light quarks, are suitable probes to describe the QGP. Since they are expected to take longer to approach local kinetic equilibrium with respect to the light degrees of freedom, their in-medium dynamics remain a challenging topic.
In a recent work [8], the question of charm thermalization was tackled from a dynamical point of view, studying the hydrodynamization time of charm quarks in the context of an expanding medium.

It is shown that τn goes below τexp quite fast when using transport coefficients arising from fits to experimental data, indicating that the conditions for a fluid-dynamic description are fulfilled for a sizeable fraction of the deconfined fireball lifetime.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an expanding deconfined quark–gluon plasma (QGP) fireball produced in a high-energy heavy-ion collision. Inside this medium, charm quarks of mass m_c ≈ 1.27 GeV are produced via hard partonic scattering at early times and subsequently propagate through the plasma. Their interaction with the medium can be modeled as Brownian motion governed by a Fokker–Planck (or equivalent Langevin) equation, in which the spatial diffusion coefficient D_s(T), the momentum-space drag coefficient η_D(T), and the momentum diffusion coefficient κ(T) characterize the transport. Define:

(i) the kinetic-equilibration (or thermalization) time τ_th as the characteristic time on which the charm-quark phase-space distribution relaxes toward a local thermal distribution at the local fluid temperature T(τ);
(ii) the hydrodynamization time τ_n as the time after which the charm-quark stress–energy tensor is well approximated by its Navier–Stokes (first-order viscous hydrodynamic) form built from gradients of the local temperature and flow velocity;
(iii) the expansion (Hubble-like) time τ_exp = 1/(∂_μ u^μ) of the bulk medium, with u^μ the local fluid four-velocity.

Address the following:

(a) Quantify how closely charm quarks approach local kinetic equilibrium with the light partonic degrees of freedom during the lifetime of the QGP, as a function of T and of the transport coefficients (D_s(T), η_D(T), κ(T)), and determine the corresponding time scale τ_th relative to that of light quarks and gluons.

(b) Identify the range of values of the dimensionless diffusion coefficient 2π T D_s(T) (and equivalently of η_D and κ, related by Einstein relations) for which τ_n < τ_exp holds for a sizeable fraction of the deconfined fireball lifetime, so that a fluid-dynamic (viscous hydrodynamic) description of the charm component is internally consistent.

(c) Determine whether transport coefficients obtained from current phenomenological fits to heavy-flavor observables in heavy-ion collisions lie within this regime, and characterize the residual deviations from local equilibrium that should be expected.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent studies indicate that, using transport coefficients fit to data, the charm hydrodynamization time τ_n falls below the expansion time τ_exp for a substantial portion of the QGP lifetime, suggesting partial thermalization. However, the precise degree of charm kinetic equilibration, the temperature dependence of D_s(T), and the validity range of a fluid description for charm remain actively debated open questions in heavy-ion phenomenology.
